title: Whose is this? Whose are these? Kenen …?
focus: Ask whose one or several things are without adding a personal suffix.
prerequisiteSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences

exercises.prompt: Choose “Whose book is this?” in Finnish. Use kirja (“book”), tämä on (“this is”).
exercises.explanation: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed basic noun and tämä on.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Whose questions with kenen: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: kenen + basic noun + tämä + on

parts.formation: Kenen is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”). Several things do not by themselves change kenen.
Keep the basic singular noun without a personal suffix.
Tämä identifies one thing.
Use on with singular tämä; ask whose with kenen.

optionFeedback.Kenen kirja tämä on?: Correct: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed basic noun and tämä on.
optionFeedback.Kenen kirjansa tämä on?: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed basic noun and tämä on.
optionFeedback.Kenen kirja tämä ovat?: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed basic noun and tämä on.
optionFeedback.Kuka kirja tämä on?: Ask with kenen; keep the unsuffixed basic noun and tämä on.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: kenen + unsuffixed plural noun + nämä + ovat

parts.formation: Kenen is the owner-question form of kuka (“who”). Several things do not by themselves change kenen.
kynä + -t = kynät. No personal owner is named, so keep -t and add no personal possessive suffix.
Nämä is the plural of tämä and identifies several things.
Use ovat with plural nämä; begin the owner question with kenen, without onko.
